nodes.name: Block Count Register (Offset 006h) (Chunk 6)
nodes.description: This specification defines response type bits for SDIO commands, introducing R5b notation (not in SDIO spec) to indicate when the Host Controller must check busy status after receiving responses, such as with I/O abort commands versus standard CMD52 operations.

extras.full_text:
These bits determine Response types.
Note: In the SDIO specification, response type notation of R5b is not defined. R5 includes R5b in the SDIO specification. But R5b is defined in this specification to specify the Host Controller shall check busy after receiving response. For example, usually CMD52 is used as R5 but I/O abort command shall be used as R5b.

nodes.name: Argument 1 Register (Offset 008h) (Chunk 0)
nodes.description: The Argument 1 Register, located at offset 008h, stores the SD Command Argument parameter used in SD card communication operations.

extras.full_text: This register contains the SD Command Argument.
technical_terms: Command Not Issued By Auto CMD12 Error

nodes.name: Argument 1 Register (Offset 008h) (Chunk 1)
nodes.description: This bit in the Argument 1 Register indicates CMD line availability for the Host Controller to issue SD commands. It sets to 1 when Command register is written, clears upon command response reception, and generates a Command Complete Interrupt when transitioning from 1 to 0.

extras.full_text:
If this bit is 0, it indicates the CMD line is not in use and the Host Controller can issue a SD Command using the CMD line.

This bit is set immediately after the Command register (00Fh) is written. This bit is cleared when the command response is received. Auto CMD12 and Auto CMD23 consist of two responses. In this case, this bit is not cleared by the response of CMD12 or CMD23 but cleared by the response of a read/write command.

Status issuing Auto CMD12 is not read from this bit. So if a command is issued during Auto CMD12 operation, Host Controller shall manage to issue two commands: CMD12 and a command set by Command register.

Even if the Command Inhibit (DAT) is set to 1, commands using only the CMD line can be issued if this bit is 0. Changing from 1 to 0 generates a Command Complete Interrupt in the Normal Interrupt Status register.

If the Host Controller cannot issue the command because of a command conflict error (Refer to Command CRC Error in Section 2.2.18) or because of Command Not Issued By Auto CMD12 Error (Refer to Section 2.2.23), this bit shall remain 1 and the Command Complete is not set.
technical_terms: Command Not Issued By Auto CMD12 Error

nodes.name: Argument 1 Register (Offset 008h) (Chunk 2)
nodes.description: The Host Driver can issue CMD0, CMD12, CMD13 (memory), and CMD52 (SDIO) during busy DAT lines when Command Inhibit (CMD) is zero, while other commands require Command Inhibit (DAT) to be zero; future Physical Layer Specification updates may expand this command list.

extras.full_text: The Host Driver can issue CMD0, CMD12, CMD13 (for memory) and CMD52 (for SDIO) when the DAT lines are busy during data transfer. These commands can be issued when Command Inhibit (CMD) is set to zero. Other commands shall be issued when Command Inhibit (DAT) is set to zero. Possible changes to the Physical Layer Specification may add other commands to this list in the future.
technical_terms: Command Not Issued By Auto CMD12 Error

nodes.name: Argument 1 Register (Offset 008h) (Chunk 3)
nodes.description: The Present State Register contains asynchronously-changing fields that require stable data during system bus reads. The Host Controller must sample and hold these values during read operations to meet System Bus Interface timing specifications and ensure data stability.

extras.full_text: Some fields defined in the Present State Register change values asynchronous to the system clock. The System reads these statuses through the System Bus Interface and it may require data stable period during bus cycle. The Host Controller should sample and hold values during reads from this register according to the timing required by the System Bus Interface specification.
technical_terms: Command Not Issued By Auto CMD12 Error

nodes.name: Transfer Mode Register (Offset 00Ch) (Chunk 0)
nodes.description: The Transfer Mode Register controls data transfer operations and must be configured by the Host Driver before data transfer commands or Resume commands. The register is write-protected during active data transactions (when Command Inhibit DAT=1) to prevent data loss, and must be saved/restored during Suspend/Resume operations.

extras.full_text: This register is used to control the operation of data transfers. The Host Driver shall set this register before issuing a command which transfers data (Refer to Data Present Select in the Command register), or before issuing a Resume command. The Host Driver shall save the value of this register when the data transfer is suspended (as a result of a Suspend command) and restore it before issuing a Resume command. To prevent data loss, the Host Controller shall implement write protection for this register during data transactions. Writes to this register shall be ignored when the Command Inhibit (DAT) in the Present State register is 1.

nodes.name: Command Register (Offset 00Eh) (Chunk 0)
nodes.description: The Command Register's Auto CMD Enable field (offset 00Eh) controls automatic command issuance for multi-block transfers: Auto CMD12 automatically terminates transfers after the last block, while Auto CMD23 (requiring Host Controller v3.00+, ADMA, and CMD23-compatible cards) automatically issues CMD23 before CMD18/CMD25 commands.

extras.full_text:
Auto CMD Enable
This field determines use of auto command functions.

00b Auto Command Disabled
01b Auto CMD12 Enable
10b Auto CMD23 Enable
11b Reserved

There are two methods to stop Multiple-block read and write operation.

(1) Auto CMD12 Enable
When this field is set to 01b, the Host Controller issues CMD12 automatically when last block transfer is completed. Auto CMD12 error is indicated to the Auto CMD Error Status register.
The Host Driver shall not set this bit if the command does not require CMD12. In particular, secure commands defined in the Part 3 File Security specification do not require CMD12.

(2) Auto CMD23 Enable
When this bit field is set to 10b, the Host Controller issues a CMD23 automatically before issuing a command specified in the Command Register. The Host Controller Version 3.00 and later shall support this function. The following conditions are required to use the Auto CMD23.
• Auto CMD23 Supported (Host Controller Version is 3.00 or later)
• A memory card that supports CMD23 (SCR[33]=1)
• If DMA is used, it shall be ADMA.
• Only when CMD18 or CMD25 is issued
(Note, the Host Controller does not check command index.)

nodes.name: Command Register (Offset 00Eh) (Chunk 1)
nodes.description: The Command Register at offset 00Eh supports Auto CMD23 functionality with or without ADMA, where writing to the register triggers CMD23 followed by the indexed command; CMD23 errors halt execution of the second command and are reported in the Auto CMD Error Status register, with the 32-bit block count stored in the SDMA System Address/Argument 2 register.

extras.full_text:
Auto CMD23 can be used with or without ADMA. By writing the Command register, the Host Controller issues a CMD23 first and then issues a command specified by the Command Index in Command register. If response errors of CMD23 are detected, the second command is not issued. A CMD23 error is indicated in the Auto CMD Error Status register.
32-bit block count value for CMD23 is set to SDMA System Address / Argument 2 register.

nodes.name: Command Register (Offset 00Eh) (Chunk 2)
nodes.description: The Block Count Enable bit in the Command Register (Offset 00Eh) controls whether the Block Count register is active for multiple block transfers; when disabled (0), it enables infinite transfers or ADMA2 transfers exceeding 65535 blocks using Descriptor Table length designation.

extras.full_text:
Block Count Enable
This bit is used to enable the Block Count register, which is only relevant for multiple block transfers. When this bit is 0, the Block Count register is disabled, which is useful in executing an infinite transfer. (Refer to Table 2-8)
If ADMA2 data transfer is more than 65535 blocks, this bit shall be set to 0. In this case, data transfer length is designated by Descriptor Table.

1 Enable
0 Disable

nodes.name: Command Register (Offset 00Eh) (Chunk 3)
nodes.description: The Host Driver must verify Command Inhibit (DAT) and Command Inhibit (CMD) bits in the Present State register are clear before writing to the Command Register (Offset 00Eh), as the Host Controller provides no write protection; writing the upper byte initiates SD command generation.

extras.full_text: The Host Driver shall check the Command Inhibit (DAT) bit and Command Inhibit (CMD) bit in the Present State register before writing to this register. Writing to the upper byte of this register triggers SD command generation. The Host Driver has the responsibility to write this register because the Host Controller does not protect for writing when Command Inhibit (CMD) is set.

nodes.name: Command Register (Offset 00Eh) (Chunk 4)
nodes.description: The Command Register specifies the command index (CMD0-63, ACMD0-63) from bits 45-40 of the Physical Layer specification and defines three command types (Suspend, Resume, Abort). Suspend commands release the SD Bus for DAT line operations, de-asserting Read Wait and stopping busy checks, while failed suspends maintain state until Continue Request restarts transfer.

extras.full_text:
Command Index
These bits shall be set to the command number (CMD0-63, ACMD0-63) that is specified in bits 45-40 of the Command-Format in the Physical Layer Specification and SDIO Card Specification.

Command Type
There are three types of special commands: Suspend, Resume and Abort. These bits shall be set to 00b for all other commands.

(1) Suspend Command
If the Suspend command succeeds, the Host Controller shall assume the SD Bus has been released and that it is possible to issue the next command, which uses the DAT line. The Host Controller shall de-assert Read Wait for read transactions and stop checking busy for write transactions. The interrupt cycle shall start, in 4-bit mode. If the Suspend command fails, the Host Controller shall maintain its current state, and the Host Driver shall restart the transfer by setting Continue Request in the Block Gap Control register. (Refer to 3.12.1 Suspend Sequence)

nodes.name: Command Register (Offset 00Eh) (Chunk 5)
nodes.description: The Command Register at offset 00Eh supports Resume and Abort commands: Resume restarts data transfer by restoring registers 000-00Dh after checking busy status for writes; Abort halts buffer reads or stops DAT line writes, requiring subsequent software reset.

extras.full_text:
(2) Resume Command
The Host Driver re-starts the data transfer by restoring the registers in the range of 000-00Dh. (Refer to Figure 1-4 in section 1.6 for the register map.) The Host Controller shall check for busy before starting write transfers.
(3) Abort Command
If this command is set when executing a read transfer, the Host Controller shall stop reads to the buffer. If this command is set when executing a write transfer, the Host Controller shall stop driving the DAT line. After issuing the Abort command, the Host Driver should issue a software reset. (Refer to 3.8 Abort Transaction)

nodes.name: Command Register (Offset 00Eh) (Chunk 6)
nodes.description: The Stop At Block Gap Request bit in the Command Register controls transfer suspension for SD card read/write operations, utilizing Read Wait or clock stopping mechanisms for reads, and requires all data to be written before activation for writes, affecting transfer status bits in the Present State register.

extras.full_text:
to 1 until the Transfer Complete is set to 1. Clearing both Stop At Block Gap Request and Continue Request shall not cause the transaction to restart. When Host Controller version is 1.00, the Host Driver can set this bit if the card supports Read Wait Control. When Host Controller version is 2.00 or later, the Host Driver can set this bit regardless of the card supports Read Wait Control. The Host Controller shall stop read transfer by using Read Wait or stopping SD clock. In case of write transfers in which the Host Driver writes data to the Buffer Data Port register, the Host Driver shall set this bit after all block data is written. If this bit is set to 1, the Host Driver shall not write data to Buffer Data Port register.
This bit affects Read Transfer Active, Write Transfer Active, DAT Line Active and Command Inhibit (DAT) in the Present State register.
Regarding detailed control of bits D01 and D00, refer to Section 3.8 and 3.12.

nodes.name: Command Register (Offset 00Eh) (Chunk 7)
nodes.description: This specification defines three methods for restarting data transfer after a block gap stop in SD card operations: using Continue Request when no Suspend command is issued or when Suspend is rejected, or using Resume command when Suspend is accepted by the card.

extras.full_text:
There are three cases to restart the transfer after stop at the block gap. Which case is appropriate depends on whether the Host Controller issues a Suspend command or the SD card accepts the Suspend command.

(1) If the Host Driver does not issue a Suspend command, the Continue Request shall be used to restart the transfer.
(2) If the Host Driver issues a Suspend command and the SD card accepts it, a Resume command shall be used to restart the transfer.
(3) If the Host Driver issues a Suspend command and the SD card does not accept it, the Continue Request shall be used to restart the transfer.

Any time Stop At Block Gap Request stops the data transfer, the Host Driver shall wait for Transfer Complete (in the Normal Interrupt Status register) before attempting to restart the transfer. When restarting the data transfer by Continue Request, the Host Driver shall clear Stop At Block Gap Request before or simultaneously.

nodes.name: Response Register (Offset 010h) (Chunk 0)
nodes.description: The Response Register at offset 010h stores command responses received from SD cards during communication protocol operations.

extras.full_text: This register is used to store responses from SD cards.

nodes.name: Response Register (Offset 010h) (Chunk 1)
nodes.description: The Response Register at offset 010h contains bit positions that correspond to response values as defined in the Physical Layer Specification, enabling standardized communication protocol responses.

extras.full_text: The Response Field indicates bit positions of "Responses" defined in the Physical Layer Specification.

nodes.name: Response Register (Offset 010h) (Chunk 2)
nodes.description: The Response Register (Offset 010h) stores command response data with varying formats: 48-bit responses (R1, R3-R6) store bits R[39:8] at REP[31:0], R1b/Auto CMD responses store R[39:8] at REP[127:96], and 136-bit responses (R2) store bits R[127:8] at REP[119:0].

extras.full_text: The Table 2-12 shows that most responses with a length of 48 (R[47:0]) have 32 bits of the response data (R[39:8]) stored in the Response register at REP[31:0]. Responses of type R1b (Auto CMD12 responses) and R1 (Auto CMD23 response) have response data bits R[39:8] stored in the Response register at REP[127:96]. Responses with length 136 (R[135:0]) have 120 bits of the response data (R[127:8]) stored in the Response register at REP[119:0].

nodes.name: Response Register (Offset 010h) (Chunk 3)
nodes.description: The Response Register stores partial response data for efficient 32-bit reads, while the Host Controller automatically validates the Command Index and CRC fields based on response length (48-bit: checks R[47:1]; 136-bit: checks R[119:1]), generating error interrupts when validation fails.

extras.full_text: To be able to read the response status efficiently, the Host Controller only stores part of the response data in the Response register. This enables the Host Driver to read 32 bits of response data efficiently in one read cycle on a 32-bit bus system. Parts of the response, the Index field and the CRC, are checked by the Host Controller (as specified by the Command Index Check Enable and the Command CRC Check Enable bits in the Command register) and generate an error interrupt if an error is detected. The bit range for the CRC check depends on the response length. If the response length is 48, the Host Controller shall check R[47:1], and if the response length is 136 the Host Controller shall check R[119:1].

nodes.name: Buffer Data Port Register (Offset 020h) (Chunk 0)
nodes.description: The Host Controller uses separate Response register bit fields (REP[127:96] for Auto CMD12/CMD23, REP[31:0] for CMD_wo_DAT and data commands) to prevent response overwriting when executing concurrent multiple-block transfers and commands, while preserving unmodified register bits during partial updates.

extras.full_text:
Since the Host Controller may have a multiple block data DAT line transfer executing concurrently with a CMD_wo_DAT command, the Host Controller stores the Auto CMD12 response in the upper bits (REP[127:96]) of the Response register. The CMD_wo_DAT response is stored in REP[31:0]. This allows the Host Controller to avoid overwriting the Auto CMD12 response with the CMD_wo_DAT and vice versa.

While executing Auto CMD23, the response of CMD23 is saved to REP [127:96] and the response of multiple-block read and write command is save to REP [31:0]. The response error of CMD23 is indicated in the Auto CMD Error Status register.

When the Host Controller modifies part of the Response register, as shown in the Table 2-12, it shall preserve the unmodified bits.

nodes.name: Buffer Data Port Register (Offset 020h) (Chunk 1)
nodes.description: A 32-bit data port register located at offset 020h provides direct access to the internal buffer memory through programmed I/O operations.

extras.full_text:
32-bit data port register to access internal buffer.

Buffer can be accessed through 32-bit Data Port register.

nodes.name: Buffer Data Port Register (Offset 020h) (Chunk 2)
nodes.description: This specification describes the nine-step procedure for configuring SDMA data transfers, including setting system memory addresses, block size/count parameters, transfer mode settings (Multi/Single block, DMA enable, Auto CMD12), issuing SD commands via the Command register, and handling command completion interrupts.

extras.full_text:
(1) Data location of system memory is set to the SDMA System Address register.
(2) Set the value corresponding to the executed data byte length of one block in the Block Size register.
(3) Set the value corresponding to the executed data block count in the Block Count register in accordance with Table 2-8.
(4) Set the argument value to the Argument 1 register.
(5) Set the value to the Transfer Mode register. The host driver determines Multi / Single Block Select, Block Count Enable, Data Transfer Direction, Auto CMD12 Enable and DMA Enable. Multi / Single Block Select and Block Count Enable are determined according to Table 2-8.
(6) Set the value to the Command register.
Note: When writing to the upper byte [3] of the Command register, the SD command is issued and SDMA is started.
(7) Then wait for the Command Complete Interrupt.
(8) Write 1 to the Command Complete in the Normal Interrupt Status register to clear this bit.
(9) Read Response register and get necessary information of the issued command.

nodes.name: Buffer Data Port Register (Offset 020h) (Chunk 3)
nodes.description: This specification describes an interrupt-driven DMA transfer completion procedure where the controller polls for Transfer Complete and DMA Interrupt flags, prioritizing Transfer Complete, clearing interrupt status bits, and updating the System Address register for subsequent data transfers until completion.

extras.full_text:
(10) Wait for the Transfer Complete Interrupt and DMA Interrupt.
(11) If Transfer Complete is set 1, go to Step (14) else if DMA Interrupt is set to 1, go to Step (12).Transfer Complete is higher priority than DMA Interrupt.
(12) Write 1 to the DMA Interrupt in the Normal Interrupt Status register to clear this bit.
(13) Set the next system address of the next data position to the System Address register and go to Step (10).
(14) Write 1 to the Transfer Complete and DMA Interrupt in the Normal Interrupt Status register to clear this bit.

Note: Step (2) and Step (3) can be executed simultaneously. Step (5) and Step (6) can also be executed simultaneously.

nodes.name: Present State Register (Offset 024h) (Chunk 0)
nodes.description: The Present State Register at offset 024h is a 32-bit read-only register that enables the Host Driver to retrieve the current operational status of the Host Controller.

extras.full_text: The Host Driver can get status of the Host Controller from this 32-bit read only register.

nodes.name: Present State Register (Offset 024h) (Chunk 1)
nodes.description: The Present State Register at offset 024h provides real-time signal level monitoring for CMD and DAT[3:0] lines, enabling error recovery and debugging capabilities, with particular utility in detecting busy signals on DAT[0] line.

extras.full_text:
CMD Line Signal Level
This status is used to check the CMD line level to recover from errors, and for debugging.

DAT[3:0] Line Signal Level
This status is used to check the DAT line level to recover from errors, and for debugging. This is especially useful in detecting the busy signal level from DAT[0].

nodes.name: Present State Register (Offset 024h) (Chunk 2)
nodes.description: The Present State Register at offset 024h contains a Write Protect Switch Pin Level bit that reflects the SDWP# pin status for memory and combo cards, where 1 indicates write enabled (SDWP#=1) and 0 indicates write protected (SDWP#=0).

extras.full_text:
Write Protect Switch Pin Level
The Write Protect Switch is supported for memory and combo cards. This bit reflects the SDWP# pin.

1
Write enabled (SDWP#=1)
0
Write protected (SDWP#=0)

nodes.name: Present State Register (Offset 024h) (Chunk 3)
nodes.description: The Card Detect Pin Level bit reflects the inverted SDCD# pin state without hardware debouncing, where 1 indicates card present (SDCD#=0) and 0 indicates no card (SDCD#=1); software debouncing is required for reliable card detection testing.

extras.full_text:
Card Detect Pin Level

This bit reflects the inverse value of the SDCD# pin. Debouncing is not performed on this bit. This bit may be valid when Card State Stable is set to 1, but it is not guaranteed because of propagation delay. Use of this bit is limited to testing since it must be debounced by software.

1
Card present (SDCD#=0)
0
No card present (SDCD#=1)

nodes.name: Present State Register (Offset 024h) (Chunk 4)
nodes.description: The Present State Register contains two card detection bits: Card Detect Pin Level Stable (indicates pin stability for reliable card detection) and Card Inserted (debounced signal that triggers insertion/removal interrupts). Both bits are unaffected by Software Reset For All operations.

extras.full_text:
This bit is used for testing. If it is 0, the Card Detect Pin Level is not stable. If this bit is set to 1, it means the Card Detect Pin Level is stable. No Card state can be detected by this bit is set to 1 and Card Inserted is set to 0. The Software Reset For All in the Software Reset register shall not affect this bit.

This bit indicates whether a card has been inserted. The Host Controller shall debounce this signal so that the Host Driver will not need to wait for it to stabilize. Changing from 0 to 1 generates a Card Insertion interrupt in the Normal Interrupt Status register and changing from 1 to 0 generates a Card Removal interrupt in the Normal Interrupt Status register. The Software Reset For All in the Software Reset register shall not affect this bit.

nodes.name: Present State Register (Offset 024h) (Chunk 5)
nodes.description: The Present State Register specifies host controller behavior during card insertion/removal events, requiring immediate clearing of SD Bus Power and Clock Enable bits, tri-stating CMD and DAT lines when transitioning from inserted to removed state, and implementing a debouncing state machine to ensure stable card detection signal validation.

extras.full_text:
If a card is removed while its power is on and its clock is oscillating, the Host Controller shall clear SD Bus Power in the Power Control register (Refer to Section 2.2.11) and SD Clock Enable in the Clock Control register (Refer to Section 2.2.14). When this bit is changed from 1 to 0, the Host Controller shall immediately stop driving CMD and DAT[3:0] (tri-state). In addition, the Host Driver should clear the Host Controller by the Software Reset For All in Software Reset register. The card detect is active regardless of the SD Bus Power.

Implementation Note: The Host Controller starts in "Reset" state at power on and changes to the "Debouncing" state once the debouncing clock is valid. In the "Debouncing" state, if the Host Controller detects that the signal (SDCD#) is stable during the debounce period, the state shall change to "Card Inserted" or "No Card". If the card is removed while in the "Card Inserted" state, it will immediately change to the "Debouncing" state. Since the card detect signal is then not stable, the Host Controller will change to the "Debouncing" state.

nodes.name: Present State Register (Offset 024h) (Chunk 6)
nodes.description: This specification defines the Present State Register's handling of SD Bus data transfers, including transfer completion detection when the last data block is sent, block gap suspension using Read Wait signaling for read operations, and write transaction status monitoring that triggers Transfer Complete interrupts upon completion.

extras.full_text:
(1) When the end bit of the last data block is sent from the SD Bus to the Host Controller. In case of ADMA2, the last block is designated by the last transfer of Descriptor Table.
(2) When a read transfer is stopped at the block gap initiated by a Stop At Block Gap Request.

The Host Controller shall stop read operation at the start of the interrupt cycle of the next block gap by driving Read Wait or stopping SD clock. If the Read Wait signal is already driven (due to data buffer cannot receive data), the Host Controller can continue to stop read operation by driving the Read Wait signal. It is necessary to support Read Wait in order to use suspend / resume function.

(b) In the case of write transactions
This status indicates that a write transfer is executing on the SD Bus. Changing this value from 1 to 0 generate a Transfer Complete interrupt in the Normal Interrupt Status register. Refer to Section 3.12.4 for sequence details.

nodes.name: Present State Register (Offset 024h) (Chunk 7)
nodes.description: The Write Transfer Active bit is set after a write command's end bit or when continuing a write transfer, and cleared when the SD card releases write busy signal after the last data block (or 8 SD clocks if no busy signal) or when busy is released due to a Block Gap Request.

extras.full_text:
This bit shall be set in either of the following cases:
(1) After the end bit of the write command.
(2) When writing to 1 to Continue Request in the Block Gap Control register to continue a write transfer.
This bit shall be cleared in either of the following cases:
(1) When the SD card releases write busy of the last data block. If SD card does not drive busy signal for 8 SD Clocks, the Host Controller shall consider the card drive "Not Busy". In case of ADMA2, the last block is designated by the last transfer of Descriptor Table.
(2) When the SD card releases write busy prior to waiting for write transfer as a result of a Stop At Block Gap Request.

nodes.name: Present State Register (Offset 024h) (Chunk 8)
nodes.description: The Command with Busy status bit indicates when a busy-generating command (e.g., memory erase) is executing on the SD Bus; it sets after the command's end bit, clears when busy de-asserts, and generates a Transfer Complete interrupt upon transitioning from 1 to 0.

extras.full_text:
(c) Command with busy
This status indicates whether a command indicates busy (ex. erase command for memory) is executing on the SD Bus. This bit is set after the end bit of the command with busy and cleared when busy is de-asserted. Changing this bit from 1 to 0 generate a Transfer Complete interrupt in the Normal Interrupt Status register. Refer Figure 2-11 to Figure 2-13.

1 DAT Line Active
0 DAT Line Inactive

nodes.name: Present State Register (Offset 024h) (Chunk 9)
nodes.description: The Command Inhibit (DAT) status bit indicates whether the Host Controller can issue SD Commands using the DAT line; when set to 1, commands cannot be issued due to active DAT line or read transfer, and transitioning from 1 to 0 triggers a Transfer Complete interrupt.

extras.full_text:
01 ROC
Command Inhibit (DAT)
This status bit is generated if either the DAT Line Active or the Read Transfer Active is set to 1. If this bit is 0, it indicates the Host Controller can issue the next SD Command. Commands with busy signal belong to Command Inhibit (DAT) (ex. R1b, R5b type). Changing from 1 to 0 generates a Transfer Complete interrupt in the Normal Interrupt Status register.
Note: The SD Host Driver can save registers in the range of 000-00Dh for a suspend transaction after this bit has changed from 1 to 0.

1 Cannot issue command which uses the DAT line
0 Can issue command which uses the DAT line

nodes.name: Host Control 1 Register (Offset 028h) (Chunk 0)
nodes.description: This Host Control 1 Register bit controls card detection source selection between SDCD# signal (normal operation) and Card Detect Test Level (testing), with a requirement to disable interrupts during switching to prevent glitch-induced false triggers.

extras.full_text:
This bit selects source for the card detection.

1
The Card Detect Test Level is selected
(for test purpose)
0
SDCD# is selected (for normal use)

When the source for the card detection is switched, the interrupt should be disabled during the switching period by clearing the Interrupt Status/Signal Enable register in order to mask unexpected interrupt being caused by the glitch. The Interrupt Status/Signal Enable should be disabled during over the period of debouncing.

This bit is enabled while the Card Detect Signal Selection is set to 1 and it indicates card inserted or not.

1
Card Inserted
0
No Card

nodes.name: Host Control 1 Register (Offset 028h) (Chunk 1)
nodes.description: This bit enables 8-bit bus width mode for embedded devices when supported (indicated in Capabilities register), otherwise bus width defaults to the Data Transfer Width setting; however, when multiple devices share a bus slot, the Shared Bus Control register's Bus Width Preset field controls individual device widths instead.

extras.full_text:
This bit controls 8-bit bus width mode for embedded device. Support of this function is indicated in 8-bit Support for Embedded Device in the Capabilities register. If a device supports 8-bit bus mode, this bit may be set to 1. If this bit is 0, bus width is controlled by Data Transfer Width in the Host Control 1 register. This bit is not effective when multiple devices are installed on a bus slot (Slot Type is set to 10b in the Capabilities register). In this case, each device bus width is controlled by Bus Width Preset field in the Shared Bus Control register.

1
8-bit Bus Width
0
Bus Width is Selected by Data Transfer Width

nodes.name: Host Control 1 Register (Offset 028h) (Chunk 2)
nodes.description: The Host Control 1 Register (Offset 028h) allows selection of DMA modes (SDMA or 32-bit Address ADMA2) after verifying support via the Capabilities register, with actual DMA usage controlled by the Transfer Mode register's DMA Enable bit.

extras.full_text:
One of supported DMA modes can be selected. The host driver shall check support of DMA modes by referring the Capabilities register. Use of selected DMA is determined by DMA Enable of the Transfer Mode register.

00
SDMA is selected
01
Reserved (New assignment is not allowed)
10
32-bit Address ADMA2 is selected
11
Reserved (will be modified by Version 4.00)

nodes.name: Host Control 1 Register (Offset 028h) (Chunk 3)
nodes.description: The High Speed Enable bit controls SD card signal timing: when cleared (default), CMD and DAT lines output at clock falling edge up to 25MHz; when set, they output at rising edge up to 50MHz, requiring SD Clock Enable reset if Preset Value Enable is active to prevent clock glitches.

extras.full_text:
High Speed Enable
This bit is optional. Before setting this bit, the Host Driver shall check the High Speed Support in the Capabilities register. If this bit is set to 0 (default), the Host Controller outputs CMD line and DAT lines at the falling edge of the SD Clock (up to 25MHz). If this bit is set to 1, the Host Controller outputs CMD line and DAT lines at the rising edge of the SD Clock (up to 50MHz).

If Preset Value Enable in the Host Control 2 register is set to 1, Host Driver needs to reset SD Clock Enable before changing this field to avoid generating clock glitches. After setting this field, the Host Driver sets SD Clock Enable again.

nodes.name: Host Control 1 Register (Offset 028h) (Chunk 4)
nodes.description: The Host Control 1 Register (Offset 028h) Data Transfer Width bit allows the host driver to configure the host controller's data width to match the connected SD card's data width specification.

extras.full_text:
Data Transfer Width
This bit selects the data width of the Host Controller. The Host Driver shall set it to match the data width of the SD card.

nodes.name: Host Control 1 Register (Offset 028h) (Chunk 5)
nodes.description: The LED Control bit in the Host Control 1 Register (Offset 028h) signals user caution during SD card access, preventing card removal during transactions. Software can maintain this bit set across multiple SD commands without requiring changes between individual transactions.

extras.full_text:
LED Control
This bit is used to caution the user not to remove the card while the SD card is being accessed. If the software is going to issue multiple SD commands, this bit can be set during all these transactions. It is not necessary to change for each transaction.

nodes.name: Host Control 1 Register (Offset 028h) (Chunk 6)
nodes.description: The Command Complete bit in the Host Control 1 Register sets when a command response end bit is received, except for Auto CMD12/23 where completion is determined by the read/write command response. Command Timeout Error takes priority over Command Complete when both occur simultaneously.

extras.full_text:
This bit is set when get the end bit of the command response. Auto CMD12 and Auto CMD23 consist of two responses. Command Complete is not generated by the response of CMD12 or CMD23 but generated by the response of a read/write command.
Refer to Command Inhibit (CMD) in the Present State register for how to control this bit.

The table below shows that Command Timeout Error has higher priority than Command Complete. If both bits are set to 1, it can be considered that the response was not received correctly.

nodes.name: Power Control Register (Offset 029h) (Chunk 0)
nodes.description: The Power Control Register (Offset 029h) enables the Host Driver to select and control SD card voltage levels by checking Capabilities register support before application. The register controls SD Bus power state, automatically clearing when no card is detected and tri-stating CMD/DAT lines while driving SDCLK low upon power-off.

extras.full_text:
By setting these bits, the Host Driver selects the voltage level for the SD card. Before setting this register, the Host Driver shall check the Voltage Support bits in the Capabilities register. If an unsupported voltage is selected, the Host System shall not supply SD Bus voltage.

Before setting this bit, the SD Host Driver shall set SD Bus Voltage Select. If the Host Controller detects the No Card state, this bit shall be cleared. If this bit is cleared, the Host Controller shall immediately stop driving CMD and DAT[3:0] (tri-state) and drive SDCLK to low level (Refer to Section 2.2.14).

nodes.name: Power Control Register (Offset 029h) (Chunk 1)
nodes.description: The Host Driver must supply appropriate SD Bus voltage based on SD card OCR and system capabilities through the Power Control Register at offset 029h. The Host Controller will ignore SD Bus Power writes and maintain zero value if an unsupported voltage is selected in the SD Bus Voltage Select field.

extras.full_text:
Implementation Note:
The Host Driver has responsibility to supply SD Bus voltage by SD Bus Power, according to SD card OCR and supply voltage capabilities depend on the Host System.
If the Host Driver selects an unsupported voltage in the SD Bus Voltage Select field, the Host Controller may ignore writes to SD Bus Power and keep its value at zero.

nodes.name: Power Control Register (Offset 029h) (Chunk 2)
nodes.description: The Power Control Register at offset 029h controls SD Bus power supply, where a value of 0 prohibits power delivery and a value of 1 permits power delivery based on system conditions such as remaining battery capacity.

extras.full_text:
Implementation Note:
The Host System shall not supply SD Bus power when SD Bus Power is set to 0 and can supply SD Bus power when SD Bus Power is set to 1 depending on the system conditions (ex. Left of the battery).

nodes.name: Power Control Register (Offset 029h) (Chunk 3)
nodes.description: This specification describes ADMA (Advanced DMA) configuration for data transfer, including setting up descriptor tables, block size/count registers, and transfer mode control. When Block Count Enable is disabled, transfer length is determined solely by the Descriptor Table, with excess data being discarded upon completion.

extras.full_text:
(1) Create Descriptor table for ADMA in the system memory
(2) Set the Descriptor address for ADMA in the ADMA System Address register.
(3) Set the value corresponding to the executed data byte length of one block in the Block Size register.
(4) Set the value corresponding to the executed data block count in the Block Count register in accordance with Table 2-8.

If the Block Count Enable in the Transfer Mode register is set to 1, total data length can be designated by the Block Count register and the Descriptor Table. These two parameters shall indicate same data length. However, transfer length is limited by the Block Count register.
If the Block Count Enable in the Transfer Mode register is set to 0, total data length is designated by not Block Count register but the Descriptor Table. In this case, ADMA reads more data than length programmed in descriptor from SD card. Too much read operation is aborted asynchronously and extra read data is discarded when the ADMA is completed

nodes.name: Power Control Register (Offset 029h) (Chunk 4)
nodes.description: This specification details the SD card command execution sequence, including setting argument and transfer mode registers, issuing commands via the Command register upper byte, monitoring Command Complete and Transfer Complete interrupts, reading response data, and handling ADMA errors during DMA-enabled data transfers.

extras.full_text:
(5) Set the argument value to the Argument 1 register.
(6) Set the value to the Transfer Mode register. The host driver determines Multi / Single Block Select, Block Count Enable, Data Transfer Direction, Auto CMD12 Enable and DMA Enable. Multi / Single Block Select and Block Count Enable are determined according to Table 2-8.
(7) Set the value to the Command register.
Note: When writing to the upper byte [3] of the Command register, the SD command is issued and DMA is started.
(8) Then wait for the Command Complete Interrupt.
(9) Write 1 to the Command Complete in the Normal Interrupt Status register to clear this bit.
(10) Read Response register and get necessary information of the issued command.
(11) Wait for the Transfer Complete Interrupt and ADMA Error Interrupt.
(12) If Transfer Complete is set 1, go to Step (13) else if ADMA Error Interrupt is set to 1, go to Step (14).

nodes.name: Power Control Register (Offset 029h) (Chunk 5)
nodes.description: This specification describes the interrupt clearing and error handling sequence for ADMA operations, requiring writing 1 to Transfer Complete and ADMA Error Status registers, followed by aborting ADMA operation and issuing SD card abort commands while checking the ADMA Error Status register.

extras.full_text:
(13) Write 1 to the Transfer Complete Status in the Normal Interrupt Status register to clear this bit.
(14) Write 1 to the ADMA Error Interrupt Status in the Error Interrupt Status register to clear this bit.
(15) Abort ADMA operation. SD card operation should be stopped by issuing abort command. If necessary, the host driver checks ADMA Error Status register to detect why ADMA error is generated.

Note: Step (3) and Step (4) can be executed simultaneously. Step (6) and Step (7) can also be executed simultaneously.

nodes.name: Block Gap Control Register (Offset 02Ah) (Chunk 0)
nodes.description: This bit enables (1) or disables (0) interrupt detection at block gaps during multiple block transfers in 4-bit SDIO mode, with the setting determined by the card's CCCR register upon insertion.

extras.full_text: This bit is valid only in 4-bit mode of the SDIO card and selects a sample point in the interrupt cycle. Setting to 1 enables interrupt detection at the block gap for a multiple block transfer. Setting to 0 disables interrupt detection during a multiple block transfer. If the SD card cannot signal an interrupt during a multiple block transfer, this bit should be set to 0. When the Host Driver detects an SD card insertion, it shall set this bit according to the CCCR of the SDIO card.

nodes.name: Block Gap Control Register (Offset 02Ah) (Chunk 1)
nodes.description: The Block Gap Control Register's read wait function bit (offset 02Ah) enables SDIO cards to stop read data via DAT[2] line if supported, otherwise the SD Clock must be stopped. The Host Driver must verify card support via CCCR before enabling; improper configuration causes DAT line conflicts and prevents Suspend/Resume functionality.

extras.full_text: The read wait function is optional for SDIO cards. If the card supports read wait, set this bit to enable use of the read wait protocol to stop read data using the DAT[2] line. Otherwise, the Host Controller has to stop the SD Clock to hold read data, which restricts commands generation. When the Host Driver detects an SD card insertion, it shall set this bit according to the CCCR of the SDIO card. If the card does not support read wait, this bit shall never be set to 1 otherwise DAT line conflict may occur. If this bit is set to 0, Suspend/Resume cannot be supported.

nodes.name: Block Gap Control Register (Offset 02Ah) (Chunk 2)
nodes.description: The Continue Request bit in the Block Gap Control Register restarts a previously stopped data transfer transaction. The Host Controller automatically clears this bit when DAT Line Active (read) or Write Transfer Active (write) transitions from 0 to 1, making manual clearing unnecessary unless Stop At Block Gap Request is set.

extras.full_text:
This bit is used to restart a transaction, which was stopped using the Stop At Block Gap Request. To cancel stop at the block gap, set Stop At Block Gap Request to 0 and set this bit 1 to restart the transfer.

The Host Controller automatically clears this bit in either of the following cases:

(1) In the case of a read transaction, the DAT Line Active changes from 0 to 1 as a read transaction restarts.

(2) In the case of a write transaction, the Write Transfer Active changes from 0 to 1 as the write transaction restarts.

Therefore, it is not necessary for Host Driver to set this bit to 0. If Stop At Block Gap Request is set to 1, any write to this bit is ignored.

nodes.name: Block Gap Control Register (Offset 02Ah) (Chunk 3)
nodes.description: The Block Gap Control Register at offset 02Ah halts read/write transactions at the next block boundary for non-DMA, SDMA, and ADMA transfers, with the Host Driver required to maintain the bit in its set state.

extras.full_text: This bit is used to stop executing read and write transaction at the next block gap for non-DMA, SDMA and ADMA transfers. The Host Driver shall leave this bit set

nodes.name: Wakeup Control Register (Offset 02Bh) (Chunk 0)
nodes.description: The Wakeup Control Register (Offset 02Bh) is mandatory for Host Controllers, though wakeup functionality depends on system hardware/software implementation. To enable wakeup events via Card Interrupt, the Host Driver must maintain SD Bus voltage by setting SD Bus Power to 1 in the Power Control register.

extras.full_text: This register is mandatory for the Host Controller, but wakeup functionality depends on the Host Controller system hardware and software. The Host Driver shall maintain voltage on the SD Bus, by setting SD Bus Power to 1 in the Power Control register, when wakeup event via Card Interrupt is desired.

nodes.name: Wakeup Control Register (Offset 02Bh) (Chunk 1)
nodes.description: The Wakeup Control Register at offset 02Bh contains a read/write-1-to-clear Command End Bit Error flag (bit 02) that is set when the command response end bit is incorrectly detected as 0 instead of the expected 1, indicating a communication error.

extras.full_text:
02
RW1C
Command End Bit Error
This bit is set when detecting that the end bit of a command response is 0.

1
End Bit Error Generated
0
No Error

nodes.name: Wakeup Control Register (Offset 02Bh) (Chunk 2)
nodes.description: The Command CRC Error bit (offset 02Bh, bit 01) is set when a CRC error is detected in a command response or when a CMD line conflict occurs, indicated by the Host Controller detecting a logic level mismatch during command transmission.

extras.full_text:
01
RW1C
Command CRC Error
Command CRC Error is generated in two cases.
If a response is returned and the Command Timeout Error is set to 0 (indicating no timeout), this bit is set to 1 when detecting a CRC error in the command response.
The Host Controller detects a CMD line conflict by monitoring the CMD line when a command is issued. If the Host Controller drives the CMD line to 1 level, but detects 0 level on the CMD line at the next SD clock edge, then the Host Controller shall abort the command (Stop driving CMD line) and set this bit to 1. The Command Timeout Error shall also be set to 1 to distinguish CMD line conflict (Refer to Table 2-25).

1
CRC Error Generated.
0
No Error

nodes.name: Wakeup Control Register (Offset 02Bh) (Chunk 3)
nodes.description: The Command Timeout Error bit (offset 02Bh, bit 00) is set when no SD card response is received within 64 clock cycles after a command's end bit, or immediately upon detecting a CMD line conflict with concurrent CRC error.

extras.full_text:
00
RW1C
Command Timeout Error
This bit is set only if no response is returned within 64 SD clock cycles from the end bit of the command. If the Host Controller detects a CMD line conflict, in which case Command CRC Error shall also be set as shown in Table 2-25, this bit shall be set without waiting for 64 SD clock cycles because the command will be aborted by the Host Controller.

1
Time out
0
No Error

nodes.name: Wakeup Control Register (Offset 02Bh) (Chunk 4)
nodes.description: The Wakeup Control Register at offset 02Bh defines the relationship between Command CRC Error and Command Timeout Error conditions, as detailed in Table 2-25.

extras.full_text: The relation between Command CRC Error and Command Timeout Error is shown in Table 2-25.

nodes.name: Clock Control Register (Offset 02Ch) (Chunk 0)
nodes.description: The Host Driver must configure the SDCLK Frequency Select field in the Clock Control Register (offset 02Ch) during Host Controller initialization, with the frequency value determined by specifications in the Capabilities register.

extras.full_text: At the initialization of the Host Controller, the Host Driver shall set the SDCLK Frequency Select according to the Capabilities register.
technical_terms: Base Clock Frequency For SD Clock

nodes.name: Clock Control Register (Offset 02Ch) (Chunk 1)
nodes.description: The Clock Control Register (Offset 02Ch) configures the SDCLK pin frequency through a divisor-based system in Host Controller Versions 1.00 and 2.00, supporting 8-bit Divided Clock Mode with programmable divisors ranging from base clock to base clock divided by 256.

extras.full_text:
SDCLK Frequency Select
This register is used to select the frequency of SDCLK pin. The definition of this field is dependent on the Host Controller Version.

(1) 8-bit Divided Clock Mode
This mode is supported by the Host Controller Version 1.00 and 2.00. The frequency is not programmed directly; rather this register holds the divisor of the Base Clock Frequency For SD Clock in the Capabilities register. Only the following settings are allowed.

80h base clock divided by 256
40h base clock divided by 128
20h base clock divided by 64
10h base clock divided by 32
08h base clock divided by 16
04h base clock divided by 8
02h base clock divided by 4
01h base clock divided by 2
00h Base clock (10MHz-63MHz)
technical_terms: Base Clock Frequency For SD Clock

nodes.name: Clock Control Register (Offset 02Ch) (Chunk 2)
nodes.description: The Clock Control Register configures SD Clock frequency by dividing the Base Clock using a divisor specified in bits, with default values for 400KHz, 25MHz, and 50MHz operation. Maximum frequencies are limited to 25MHz in normal speed mode and 50MHz in high speed mode per Physical Layer Specification.

extras.full_text:
Setting 00h specifies the highest frequency of the SD Clock. When setting multiple bits, the most significant bit is used as the divisor but it should not be set. The three default divider values can be calculated by the frequency that is defined by the Base Clock Frequency For SD Clock in the Capabilities register.
400KHz divider value
25MHz divider value
50MHz divider value
According to the Physical Layer Specification, the maximum SD Clock frequency is 25 MHz in normal speed mode and 50MHz in high speed mode, and shall never exceed this limit.
The frequency of SDCLK is set by the following formula:

Clock Frequency = (Base Clock) / divisor
technical_terms: Base Clock Frequency For SD Clock

nodes.name: Clock Control Register (Offset 02Ch) (Chunk 3)
nodes.description: This specification defines clock divisor selection for SD clock generation, where the smallest divisor yielding a frequency ≤ target should be chosen (e.g., 33MHz base with divisor 01h yields 16.5MHz for 25MHz target). Host Controller Version 3.00 mandates 10-bit Divided Clock Mode, extending divisor length from 8-bit with support for all values.

extras.full_text:
Thus, choose the smallest possible divisor which results in a clock frequency that is less than or equal to the target frequency.
For example, if the Base Clock Frequency For SD Clock in the Capabilities register has the value 33MHz, and the target frequency is 25MHz, then choosing the divisor value of 01h will yield 16.5MHz, which is the nearest frequency less than or equal to the target. Similarly, to approach a clock value of 400KHz, the divisor value of 40h yields the optimal clock value of 258KHz.

(2) 10-bit Divided Clock Mode
Host Controller Version 3.00 supports this mandatory mode instead of the 8-bit Divided Clock Mode. The length of divider is extended to10 bits and all divider values shall be supported.
technical_terms: Base Clock Frequency For SD Clock

nodes.name: Clock Control Register (Offset 02Ch) (Chunk 4)
nodes.description: The Programmable Clock Mode, optional in Host Controller Version 3.00, uses a Clock Multiplier value from the Capabilities register to enable finer-grain SD clock frequency selection. The clock frequency setting is either Host Driver-controlled or automatically determined by Preset Value registers, depending on the Preset Value Enable bit in Host Control 2 register.

extras.full_text:
(3) Programmable Clock Mode
Host Controller Version 3.00 supports this mode as optional. A non-zero value set to Clock Multiplier in the Capabilities register indicates support of this clock mode. The multiplier enables the Host System to select a finer grain SD clock frequency. It is not necessary to support all frequency generation specified by this field because programmable clock generator is vendor specific and dependent on the implementation. Therefore, this mode is used with Preset Value registers. The Host Controller vendor provides possible settings and the Host System vendor sets appropriate values to the Preset Value registers.

This field depends on setting of Preset Value Enable in the Host Control 2 register.
If Preset Value Enable = 0, this field is set by Host Driver.
If the Preset Value Enable = 1, this field is automatically set to a value specified in one of Preset Value registers.
technical_terms: Base Clock Frequency For SD Clock

nodes.name: Clock Control Register (Offset 02Ch) (Chunk 5)
nodes.description: The Clock Control Register defines status bits for buffer read/write readiness (bits 05-04) triggered by Buffer Enable state changes, and DMA interrupt signaling (bit 03) for SDMA boundary detection and ADMA descriptor-based interrupts during data transfer operations.

extras.full_text:
05 RW1C Buffer Read Ready
This status is set if the Buffer Read Enable changes from 0 to 1. Refer to the Buffer Read Enable in the Present State register.
While performing tuning procedure (Execute Tuning is set to 1), Buffer Read Ready is set to 1 for every CMD19 execution.

1 Ready to read buffer
0 Not ready to read buffer

04 RW1C Buffer Write Ready
This status is set if the Buffer Write Enable changes from 0 to 1. Refer to the Buffer Write Enable in the Present State register.

1 Ready to write buffer
0 Not ready to write buffer

03 RW1C DMA Interrupt
This status is set if the Host Controller detects the Host SDMA Buffer boundary during transfer. Refer to the Host SDMA Buffer Boundary in the Block Size register.
Other DMA interrupt factors may be added in the future.
In case of ADMA, by setting Int field in the descriptor table, Host Controller generates this interrupt. Suppose that it is used for debugging.
This interrupt shall not be generated after the Transfer Complete.

1 DMA Interrupt is generated
0 No DMA Interrupt
technical_terms: Base Clock Frequency For SD Clock

nodes.name: Clock Control Register (Offset 02Ch) (Chunk 6)
nodes.description: The Block Gap Event bit (bit 02) in the Clock Control Register indicates when a read/write transaction has stopped at a block gap boundary, triggered by the falling edge of DAT Line Active Status for reads or Write Transfer Active Status for writes, contingent upon the Stop At Block Gap Request being enabled.

extras.full_text:
02 RW1C Block Gap Event
If the Stop At Block Gap Request in the Block Gap Control register is set, this bit is set when both a read / write transaction is stopped at a block gap. If Stop At Block Gap Request is not set to 1, this bit is not set to 1.

(1) In the case of a Read Transaction
This bit is set at the falling edge of the DAT Line Active Status (When the transaction is stopped at SD Bus timing. The Read Wait shall be supported in order to use this function. Refer to Section 3.12.3 about the detail timing.
(2) Case of Write Transaction
This bit is set at the falling edge of Write Transfer Active Status (After getting CRC status at SD Bus timing). Refer to Section 3.12.4 for more details on the sequence of events.

1 Transaction stopped at block gap
0 No Block Gap Event
technical_terms: Base Clock Frequency For SD Clock

nodes.name: Clock Control Register (Offset 02Ch) (Chunk 7)

The second is when data has stopped at the block gap and completed the data transfer by setting

the Stop At Block Gap Request in the Block Gap Control register (After valid data has been read to the Host System). Refer to Section 3.12.3 for more details on the sequence of events.

nodes.name: Clock Control Register (Offset 02Ch) (Chunk 21)
nodes.description: The Clock Control Register's Clock Pin Select field (3-bit) sequentially enables individual clock outputs (CLK[1:3]) to select devices 1-3, ensuring non-overlapping clock signals without glitches by stopping the previous clock before starting the next, with frequency and buffer strength adjustments occurring during stop intervals.

extras.full_text: Figure 2-38 shows an example timing of selecting clock pin. When Clock Pin Select is set to 000b, no clocks are generated from CLK[7:0] pins. When Clock Pin Select is set to 001b, Host Controller provides clock to only CLK[1]. This means the device 1 is selected. By setting 010b to Clock Pin Select, device 2 is selected. CLK[1] is stopped and then CLK[2] is generated. By setting 011b to Clock Pin Select, device 3 is selected. CLK[2] is stopped and then CLK[3] is generated. nodes.name: Clock Control Register (Offset 02Ch) (Chunk 22)
nodes.description: The Lock-Reset pin in eSD Version 2.10 enhances security for boot loader updates, requiring host systems to maintain constant Host interface voltage (VDDH) and avoid driving Lock-Reset high during device power-off to prevent input buffer damage. Power saving is achieved through sleep mode for eSD devices and back-end function power control for embedded SDIO.

extras.full_text:
Implementation Notes:
Lock-Reset pin is defined by eSD Version 2.10 to improve security level for updating boot loader and system codes. The Host System supporting Lock-Reset needs to consider following points.
Driving Lock-Reset to high during the device power off is not allowed to prevent protection diode of Lock-Reset input buffer from destroying. Lock-Rest signal can be driven to high after power is supplied to the device. Host interface voltage (VDDH) should be always supplied to the device. Then Host System should implement so that VDDH is not controlled by SD Bus Power bit in the Power Control register.

In case of eSD, sleep mode should be used instead of eSD device power off for saving power. Memory voltage VDDF can be off when the device is in Sleep State.
In case of SDIO, embedded SDIO can support back-end function power pin. The back-end function power can be off while IOEx=0.

nodes.name: Timeout Control Register (Offset 02Eh) (Chunk 0)

08 RW1C Auto CMD Error
Auto CMD12 and Auto CMD23 use this error status. This bit is set when detecting that one of the bits D00-D04 in Auto CMD Error Status register has changed from 0 to 1. nodes.name: Timeout Control Register (Offset 02Eh) (Chunk 1)
nodes.description: The Current Limit Error bit (bit 07, RW1C) in the Timeout Control Register indicates whether the Host Controller has stopped power supply to the SD card due to current limit protection; a value of 1 signals power failure while 0 indicates normal operation.

extras.full_text:
07 RW1C Current Limit Error
By setting the SD Bus Power bit in the Power Control register, the Host Controller is requested to supply power for the SD Bus. If the Host Controller supports the Current Limit function, it can be protected from an illegal card by stopping power supply to the card in which case this bit indicates a failure status. Reading 1 means the Host Controller is not supplying power to SD card due to some failure. Reading 0 means that the Host Controller is supplying power and no error has occurred. The Host Controller may require some sampling time to detect the current limit. If the Host Controller does not support this function, this bit shall always be set to 0.

1 Power fail
0 No Error

nodes.name: Timeout Control Register (Offset 02Eh) (Chunk 16)
nodes.description: This register bit controls sampling clock selection for CMD and DAT reception, where 1 indicates successful tuning completion using a tuned clock and 0 indicates fixed clock usage or tuning failure. Host Controller uses this bit to select sampling clock to receive CMD and DAT. This bit is set by tuning procedure and valid after the completion of tuning (when Execute Tuning is cleared). Setting 1 means that tuning is completed successfully and setting 0 means that tuning is failed. Writing 1 to this bit is meaningless and ignored. A tuning circuit is reset by writing to 0. This bit can be cleared with setting Execute Tuning. Once the tuning circuit is reset, it will take time to complete tuning sequence. Therefore, Host Driver should keep this bit to 1 to perform re-tuning sequence to compete re-tuning sequence in a short time. Change of this bit is not allowed while the Host Controller is receiving response or a read data block. Refer to Figure 2-29.

0
Fixed clock is used to sample data

nodes.name: Software Reset Register (Offset 02Fh) (Chunk 0)
nodes.description: This bit indicates the Host Controller's inability to issue Auto CMD12 for stopping memory multiple block data transfers due to errors, rendering other error status bits (D04-D01) meaningless when set to 1; it remains 0 for Auto CMD23-generated errors.

If memory multiple block data transfer is not started due to command error, this bit is not set because it is not necessary to issue Auto CMD12. Setting this bit to 1 means the Host Controller cannot issue Auto CMD12 to stop memory multiple block data transfer due to some error. If this bit is set to 1, other error status bits (D04-D01) are meaningless.
This bit is set to 0 when Auto CMD Error is generated by Auto CMD23.
technical_terms: Command Not Issued By Auto CMD12 Error

nodes.name: Software Reset Register (Offset 02Fh) (Chunk 1)
nodes.description: This specification defines the Auto CMD Error Status register timing and error detection for three scenarios: issuing Auto CMD12 (checking previous command errors), receiving Auto CMD12 responses (validating response error bits D01-D04), and reading Auto CMD Error Status bit D07 (verifying command issuance capability).

extras.full_text:
The relation between Auto CMD CRC Error and Auto CMD Timeout Error is shown in Table 2-31 :.

The timing of changing Auto CMD Error Status can be classified in three scenarios:

(1) When the Host Controller is going to issue Auto CMD12
Set D00 to 1 if Auto CMD12 cannot be issued due to an error in the previous command.
Set D00 to 0 if Auto CMD12 is issued.
(2) At the end bit of an Auto CMD12 response
Check received responses by checking the error bits D01, D02, D03 and D04.
Set to 1 if error is detected.
Set to 0 if error is not detected.
(3) Before reading the Auto CMD Error Status bit D07
Set D07 to 1 if there is a command cannot be issued
Set D07 to 0 if there is no command to issue
technical_terms: Command Not Issued By Auto CMD12 Error

nodes.name: Software Reset Register (Offset 02Fh) (Chunk 2)
nodes.description: The Auto CMD Error Status register generates interrupts when error bits D00-D04 are set, with optimal D07 sampling occurring before reading the register due to asynchronous timing between Auto CMD Error generation and Command register writes; the Command Not Issued By Auto CMD12 Error (D01-D04) does not trigger separate interrupts.

extras.full_text:
Timing of generating the Auto CMD Error and writing to the Command register are asynchronous. Then D07 shall be sampled when driver never writing to the Command register. So just before reading the Auto CMD Error Status register is good timing to set the D07 status bit.

An Auto CMD Error Interrupt is generated when one of the error bits D00 to D04 is set to 1. The Command Not Issued By Auto CMD12 Error does not make any effect on interrupt because it is set when one of bits D01 to D04 is set to 1.
technical_terms: Command Not Issued By Auto CMD12 Error

nodes.name: Software Reset Register (Offset 02Fh) (Chunk 3)

extras.full_text: A reset pulse is generated when writing 1 to each bit of this register. After completing the reset, the Host Controller shall clear each bit. Because it takes some time to complete software reset, the SD Host Driver shall confirm that these bits are 0.

nodes.name: Software Reset Register (Offset 02Fh) (Chunk 4)
nodes.description: The Software Reset Register (Offset 02Fh) resets the data circuit and DMA circuit, clearing the Buffer Data Port register, specific Present State register bits (Buffer Read/Write Enable, Transfer Active states, DAT Line Active, Command Inhibit), Block Gap Control register fields, and Normal Interrupt Status register flags.

Only part of data circuit is reset. DMA circuit is also reset.

The following registers and bits are cleared by this bit:

Buffer Data Port register

Buffer is cleared and initialized.

Present State register

Buffer Read Enable

Buffer Write Enable

Read Transfer Active

Write Transfer Active

DAT Line Active

Command Inhibit (DAT)

Continue Request

Stop At Block Gap Request

Normal Interrupt Status register

Buffer Read Ready

Buffer Write Ready

DMA Interrupt

Block Gap Event

Transfer Complete
technical_terms: Command Not Issued By Auto CMD12 Error

nodes.name: Normal Interrupt Status Register (Offset 030h) (Chunk 0)
nodes.description: The Normal Interrupt Status Register generates interrupts when enabled status bits are set to 1. Status bits are cleared by writing 1 to RW1C attributes, while ROC attributes remain unchanged. The Card Interrupt clears automatically when the Card Driver services the interrupt condition.

extras.full_text: The Normal Interrupt Status Enable affects reads of this register, but Normal Interrupt Signal Enable does not affect these reads. An interrupt is generated when the Normal Interrupt Signal Enable is enabled and at least one of the status bits is set to 1. Writing 1 to a bit of RW1C attribute clears it; writing 0 keeps the bit unchanged. Writing 1 to a bit of ROC attribute keeps the bit unchanged. More than one status can be cleared with a single register write. The Card Interrupt is cleared when the card stops asserting the interrupt; that is, when the Card Driver services the interrupt condition.

nodes.name: Normal Interrupt Status Register (Offset 030h) (Chunk 1)
nodes.description: The Normal Interrupt Status Register (Offset 030h) contains a read-only Error Interrupt bit that consolidates all Error Interrupt Status register bits for efficient error checking, and a Re-Tuning Event bit that signals when the Host Driver must perform re-tuning before the next data transfer.

extras.full_text:
Error Interrupt
If any of the bits in the Error Interrupt Status register are set, then this bit is set. Therefore the Host Driver can efficiently test for an error by checking this bit first. This bit is read only.

1
Error
0
No Error

Reserved

Re-Tuning Event
This status is set if Re-Tuning Request in the Present State register changes from 0 to 1. Host Controller requests Host Driver to perform re-tuning for next data transfer. Current data transfer (not large block count) can be completed without re-tuning.

1
Re-Tuning should be performed
0
Re-Tuning is not required

nodes.name: Normal Interrupt Status Register (Offset 030h) (Chunk 2)

INT_C
This status is set if INT_C is enabled and INT_C# pin is in low level. Writing this bit to 1 does not clear this bit. It is cleared by resetting the INT_C interrupt factor. Refer to the Shared Bus Control register.

1

nodes.name: Error Interrupt Status Register (Offset 032h) (Chunk 0)
nodes.description: The Error Interrupt Status Register (Offset 032h) requires both the Error Interrupt Status Enable and Error Interrupt Signal Enable registers to generate interrupts when status bits are set. Status bits are write-1-to-clear, write-0-to-preserve, with support for clearing multiple bits in a single write operation.

extras.full_text: Signals defined in this register can be enabled by the Error Interrupt Status Enable register, but not by the Error Interrupt Signal Enable register. The interrupt is generated when the Error Interrupt Signal Enable is enabled and at least one of the statuses is set to 1. Writing to 1 clears the bit and writing to 0 keeps the bit unchanged. More than one status can be cleared at the one register write.

nodes.name: Error Interrupt Status Register (Offset 032h) (Chunk 1)
nodes.description: The Error Interrupt Status Register (Offset 032h) defines error status bits, including vendor-specific fields and a Tuning Error bit that indicates unrecoverable tuning circuit errors outside tuning procedures, requiring command abortion, data transfer retry, and resetting the sampling clock to 0.

extras.full_text:
Vendor Specific Error Status

Additional status bits can be defined in this register by the vendor.

Reserved

Tuning Error

This bit is set when an unrecoverable error is detected in a tuning circuit except during tuning procedure (Occurrence of an error during tuning procedure is indicated by Sampling Select). By detecting Tuning Error, Host Driver needs to abort a command executing and perform tuning. To reset tuning circuit, Sampling Clock shall be set to 0 before executing tuning procedure (Refer to Figure 2-29). The Tuning Error is higher priority than the other error interrupts generated during data transfer. By detecting Tuning Error, the Host Driver should discard data transferred by a current read/write command and retry data transfer after the Host Controller retrieved from tuning circuit error.

1 Error
0 No Error

nodes.name: Error Interrupt Status Register (Offset 032h) (Chunk 2)
nodes.description: The ADMA Error bit in the Error Interrupt Status Register (Offset 032h) indicates errors during ADMA data transfer, with error states saved in the ADMA Error Status Register. It triggers when invalid descriptor data (Valid=0) is detected at ST_FDS state, allowing the Host Driver to identify the error descriptor.

extras.full_text:
ADMA Error

This bit is set when the Host Controller detects errors during ADMA based data transfer. The state of the ADMA at an error occurrence is saved in the ADMA Error Status Register,

In addition, the Host Controller generates this Interrupt when it detects invalid descriptor data (Valid=0) at the ST_FDS state. ADMA Error State in the ADMA Error Status indicates that an error occurs in ST_FDS state. The Host Driver may find that Valid bit is not set at the error descriptor.

1 Error
0 No Error

nodes.name: Error Interrupt Status Register (Offset 032h) (Chunk 3)
nodes.description: This field selects one of seven available clock pin outputs (CLK[1] through CLK[7]) or disables clock pins entirely (000b), with selection of unsupported pins having no effect; timing specifications are detailed in Figure 2-38.

extras.full_text:
One of clock pin outputs is selected by this field. Select of unsupported clock pin is meaningless. Refer to Figure 2-38 for the timing of clock outputs.

000b Clock Pins are Disabled
001b CLK[1] is Selected
010b CLK[2] is Selected
...... ..........
111b CLK[7] is Selected

nodes.name: Error Interrupt Status Register (Offset 032h) (Chunk 4)
nodes.description: This register configures bus width (4-bit or 8-bit) for up to 7 embedded devices on a shared bus configuration, with bits D24-D30 individually controlling each device's data transfer width when Slot Type is set to 10b in the Capabilities register.

extras.full_text:
Shared bus supports mixing of 4-bit and 8-bit bus width devices. Each bit of this field specifies the bus width for each embedded device. The number of devices supported is specified by Number of Clock Pins and a maximum of 7 devices are supported. This field is effective when multiple devices are connected to a shared bus (Slot Type is set to 10b in the Capabilities register). In the other case, Extended Data Transfer Width in the Host Control 1 register is used to select 8-bit bus width. As use of 1-bit mode is not intended for shared bus, Data Transfer Width in the Host Control 1 register should be set to 1.

D24 Bus Width Preset for Device 1
D25 Bus Width Preset for Device 2
D26 Bus Width Preset for Device 3
D27 Bus Width Preset for Device 4
D28 Bus Width Preset for Device 5
D29 Bus Width Preset for Device 6

The function of each bit is defined as follows:
0 4-bit bus width mode (Data Transfer Width = 1)

nodes.name: Error Interrupt Status Register (Offset 032h) (Chunk 5)
nodes.description: This Error Interrupt Status Register field defines support for three asynchronous, open-drain interrupt input pins (INT_A#, INT_B#, INT_C#) in shared bus systems, with a 2-bit encoding indicating whether no interrupts, only INTA, INTA+INTB, or all three interrupt pins are supported.

extras.full_text:
This field indicates support of interrupt input pins for shared bus system. Three asynchronous interrupt pins are defined, INT_A#, INT_B# and INT_C#. Which interrupt pin is used is determined by the system. Each one is driven by open drain and then wired or connection is possible.

00b Interrupt Input Pin is Not Supported
01b INTA is Supported
10b INTA and INTB are Supported
11b INTA, INTB and INTC are Supported

nodes.name: Auto CMD Error Status Register (Offset 03Ch) (Chunk 0)
nodes.description: This register indicates response errors for Auto CMD12 and Auto CMD23 commands at offset 03Ch, with Auto CMD23 errors specifically mapped to bits 04-01, enabling the host driver to identify specific error types when Auto CMD Error flag is set.

extras.full_text: This register is used to indicate CMD12 response error of Auto CMD12 and CMD23 response error of Auto CMD23. The Host driver can determine what kind of Auto CMD12 / CMD23 errors occur by this register. Auto CMD23 errors are indicated in bit 04-01.This register is valid only when the Auto CMD Error is set.
